verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. opportunities-casting-cx.md:316 reads 'a member wanting the chair keeps review but loses decide on that slot'; 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:200 (D-10) 'Review access and submission on the same post are mutually exclusive, and the choice is applicant-side and one-way', reinforced at :111 ('Applying revokes their review access on that post for its lifetime') and :157 (DT-09); 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:218 (D-11) 'A candidate can never triage - or see - a queue they are a candidate in', with :121 'The queue is absent, not greyed out.' The CX file also contradicts itself: :126 states 'Review/submit mutual exclusion (D-10) is enforced'. No marker on any statement. Two normative statements cannot both hold, and the product differs materially (conflicted member reads every rival's evidence vs. cannot see the queue).

opportunities-casting-cx.md:56 is quoted accurately, but the behaviour is settled three times in the owning files: 04.01.03 D-14 (:220) 'compensation never renders publicly'; its Fan Role Lens (:31) 'Also never sees the compensation badge'; 04.02.01 Fan Role Lens (:31) 'Never sees: ... compensation'; 04.02.01 :168 'No fee, no checklist, no contact'; 04.02.01 D-18 (:252) 'never derives, aggregates or badges a market rate'. 04.02.01 DT-06 (:199) confirms the price signal only as an unavoidable emergent property and explicitly REJECTS it as a feature to build, so neither reading produces an artefact. The CX clause is prose about an emergent effect inside a Role-scoping bullet, not a rendering rule; no implementer builds a Fan-visible price signal against three explicit prohibitions.

The premise is falsified by the file the finding quotes. 04.06-band-member-wanted.md:65 is a modelled state row - 'Trialling | Rehearsals happening | Both sides assessing' - inside a state table running Open -> Confidential -> Trialling -> Mutual yes -> Closed (:63-67), with actors and resolution supplied by Happy Path :44-45 ('Rehearsal, not audition. Both sides assess' -> 'Mutual yes -> membership in 01'). The 'spine has no name for it' clause is the point of the divergence table at :30-37. The triage hold vocabulary is inapplicable by construction: 04.04.01 D-05 bounds every hold's resolve-by by the post's decide-by, while 04.06 :36 declares this type 'Open-ended; runs for months' with no deadline. Also note the finding adds bold emphasis at :34 and :65 that is absent from the file.

All three quotes verified (04.01.02:47 'Unresolved and important'; 04.01.02 Q-01 at :100 'RESOLVED - yes'; opportunities-casting-cx.md:98 'the unresolved intersection'). But the stale row states the resolved behaviour itself - 'honour the invite, show the poster the mismatch' (:47) is identical to 04.01.04 D-05 (:102) and to 04.01.04's Invited-override state (:74), and even the user copy matches. The finding's own forcedInvention field concedes 'None - the behaviour is decided'. Stale labelling with zero behavioural fork; every competent implementer converges.

04.01.04 D-05 (:102) is unscoped by design, and its stated rationale is explicitly universal: 'the poster's personal knowledge of a named player outranks any criterion the system holds ... Informed override, not a hidden filter.' Nothing in the file makes the legal tier special-cased against it - D-04 (:101) states document-backed criteria are 'declared but not verified at this stage, and must be labelled as self-declared', so the platform never held a verified legal fact to waive, and the waiver is an informed override by the very party who bears the liability. The cited domain R-03 (opportunities-casting-cx.md:360) rejects only platform-initiated AUTO-loosening ('silently rewrites what the poster asked for'), which is the opposite of an explicit, disclosed, poster-authored invite. Only one reading is available.

Quote verified at 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:205 (the finding adds bold absent from the file), and no per-type fill window exists. But the behaviour is fully specified - a proactive one-tap prompt that closes every slot and fires the close-out - and only the nudge threshold is unstated. The same file establishes the governing convention two rows away: D-13 (:318) 'Intervals stated as the senior-dev call; tunable at /create-prd' and D-16's per-type table (:112) 'the senior-dev call ... tunable at /create-prd, in the same way D-13's intervals are'. A near-identical type-scoped inactivity table already exists at 04.02.01:62-66 (48h dep/session/function/crew/support, 30 days member-wanted). No product behaviour must be invented; a tuning value follows an established convention.

Both quotes verified (04.01.01:47 and :185; the finding adds bold to 'Refused above 25' that the file does not carry). They are not opposite behaviours: 'soft' here means the ceiling routes rather than dead-ends, which is exactly how the corpus uses the phrase elsewhere - opportunities-casting-cx.md:327 'The 25-slot soft ceiling (04.01.01->04.07) routes here', and CX-11's index row at :29 'the 25-slot soft ceiling routes here - past it, a post is a hiring round'. Label and behaviour co-occur in the same sentence, so the reading is fixed. Only :185 specifies behaviour, and it names a real destination (04.07) with real batch tooling; contrast D-13's genuine warn-not-block, which offers no alternative shape.

Verified against 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:225-247. Post status is declared derived and 'never set directly' (:235 header), yet the enumeration has a reachable hole: slot A Closed (terminal) + slot B Submission closed (neither accepting nor terminal) satisfies no row - Published needs a slot open, Reviewing needs one reviewing plus one open, Decided needs all decided, Submission closed requires 'no slot is terminal' (:244), Closed requires all terminal (:245). Separately the Reviewing row's trigger '>=1 slot reviewing, >=1 open' (:242) does not admit its own example 'Drums - filled. Bass - 6 applicants', which is a decided+reviewing mix. Unmarked internal inconsistency in a derived state machine; implementers must invent both the missing states and a precedence rule. Warning rather than blocking - the divergence is confined to a status label on mixed-slot posts.

Verified at 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:62-66 ('At 2x the interval it auto-tombstones ... and stops accepting submissions') and D-06 (:240). 'Tombstone' appears in no other file in the domain - the mechanism is never reconciled with the lifecycle owner. It collides with three normative statements: 04.01.01 D-16 ('The decide-by is what closes the post'), D-08 plus the post-state table headed 'status follows the slots, never set directly' (:235) which enumerates no stale state, and - decisively - opportunities-casting-cx.md CX-01 synthesis Q1 (:57-58) 'The post is owned by 04.01; 04.02 is a reader with no write-back ... it never mutates the post.' A board-owned rule that stops submissions is a write-back. 04.02.01's own cross-cut (:215) treats D-06 as load-bearing behaviour, not presentation. For a dep call posted three weeks out the two rules disagree by weeks and decide whether anyone can apply.

The count is right - 04.02.01:47-58 carries ten rows against the twelve types at 04.01.01:90-102 - but both omissions resolve deterministically from stated rules. General call's taxonomy row explicitly reads 'Poster picks; both offered | Derived - follows whichever semantics the poster picked', and the board table is organised precisely along that axis (deadline-bearing types sort by deadline and are exempt from freshness because 'the deadline is the freshness signal'; wall-clock types sort by event date), so the General call inherits whichever branch the poster selected. Open-mic/showcase slot is a venue-local wall-clock, event-date, presence type identical in every scoped property to Support slot, and every presence row in the board table retains a 24 h tombstone without exception. Derivation, not invention.

D-08 quoted accurately at 04.02.04-alert-subscriptions-delivery.md:240, and no window is stated. But the same file routes the parameter away by name: DT-03 (:198) 'This pipe is a consumer of a platform-wide notification mechanism, not an owner of one. Delivery channels, quiet hours, per-channel preferences, digests and unsubscribe are needed identically by 05, 12, 17, 19, 20, 21 and 24 ... CONFIRMED - routed to the global CX as a mechanism. What stays here is the policy', and :223 lists what that cross-cut 'must expose: ... calendar-derived quiet windows (D-08)'. The default window is a parameter of a mechanism this file explicitly does not own. Divergence is also immaterial in kind - DT-06 (:201) fixes the shape (active 23:00-01:00, asleep at 09:00), so competing implementations differ by an hour of offset, not in product behaviour.

Verified: 04.02.03-material-aware-dep-matching.md:52 and :64 both carry '[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]', and 04.02-discovery-matching-alerts-cx.md:143 and :146 carry the same marker as bare synthesis answers with no question text at all (plus :104). The target stage is provably closed - 04.02.03 Q-03 itself says 'Re-pointed from the completed /ideate-discover Step 5', as do 04.02.02 Q-04 and 04.01.02 Q-02, so the corpus knows to re-point and these were missed. No owner column, no reachable stage: the tracking is malformed, not merely present. The deferred content is real behaviour, not detail - whether a setlist change re-scores a live pool or the score is allowed to go stale, on the domain's most novel feature - and it appears nowhere in that file's Open Questions table.

The gap is real but tracked with an owner and a target, and the file routes it explicitly. 04.03.05-outbound-pitch-unsolicited.md:60 states 'Expired | Target never responded within the window | See Q-02', and Q-02 (:95) is '[OWNER] Does the disposition obligation (04.05.01) apply to unsolicited pitches? ... Rolled up canonically at 04.05 Q-02 ... | User | /create-prd'. Every derived quantity the finding lists - hold ceiling, the date shown to the pitcher, the dormancy denominator, the no-decision base - exists only if the obligation attaches, which is precisely what Q-02 decides. 04.05.01 corroborates rather than contradicts: its cross-cut at :222 labels this 'scope boundary, unresolved' and its 400-pitch edge case (:174) routes to the same question. Well-formed deferral, owner named, stage named, canonical roll-up recorded.

D-02 quoted correctly at 04.03.04-blind-review-mode.md:91 and no per-type mapping exists - but producing one now would pre-empt an owner decision. Q-01 (:99) is '[OWNER] The contradiction (CX-01): blind disables evidence entirely / evidence reduced to leaky aggregates / blind scoped to evidence-irrelevant types? ... Rolled up canonically at domain Q-08 ... | User | /create-prd', and its third option IS the type-scoping question. D-01 (:90) states the contradiction is 'retained and escalated, not resolved'. The per-type list is downstream of an owner-tracked, stage-targeted question. The taxonomy's 'five scoped properties' line (04.01.01:88) names what the discriminator exists for, not an exhaustive list of everything type-dependent - 04.01.03 D-04 and this D-02 are cited there as the same pattern applied from outside.

Verified at 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:198. The rule claims to be type-scoped over a taxonomy the corpus declares 'closed and platform-curated ... not extensible by posters' (04.01.01 D-04, :309), yet two of its four buckets are keyed on labels that taxonomy cannot emit - 'A&R' is not a type (it survives only as sweep candidate 10's outbound half inside 04.03.05), and 'urgent types' is nowhere defined as a set; a domain-wide grep finds only 04.01.02:37's parenthetical 'urgency-shaped types (dep calls)'. Five of the twelve types get no ceiling at all: function/private hire, songwriting camp invitation, support slot, open-mic/showcase slot, General call. Unlike the taxonomy's own per-type tables, no derivation principle and no tunable-at-/create-prd deferral is offered, so whether a function-gig poster may ask any question is invented at build time.

Both texts verified (04.03.03-audition-tasks-media-submission.md:59 edge case; :73 States 'Waived | Evidence threshold met'), but the file resolves the mechanism explicitly and names the rejected alternative: Q-03 (:119) 'RESOLVED - a poster-set threshold ... it is expressed once, as a threshold, rather than re-taken per candidate', citing CX-05 synthesis answer 2 at 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:152-153. The edge case's normative column agrees ('Task should be waived or reduced'); only its illustrative copy predates the resolution. On 'reduced': the decision table is normative and D-03 (:91) says 'Strong evidence should waive the audition' - waive only - and the States table models only Waived, so implementations converge on waiver. Stale copy against an explicit resolution, not a live fork.

Quotes verified (04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md D-07 :251, DT-06 :170, edge case :150; 04.04.04 D-05 :97 and Q-03 :105). Downgraded from blocking: D-05 sits in the urgent-fill file and DT-04 (:76) reasons entirely about burning a cascade list, so the platform-set fuse is fairly read as cascade-scoped and the two decisions can coexist. What survives is a genuine unfilled gap with mis-routed tracking. 04.04.03's irrevocability rests wholly on the poster having chosen the window ('a window they chose', :251; 'a shorter fuse' as the poster's honest instrument, :150), DT-06 names the harm - 'a poster-set fuse with no ceiling lets a poster impose an unbounded free option on the candidate' - and hands the bound to 04.04.04 Q-03, which resolved the cascade case only and deferred just the tier-to-minutes table to /write-be-spec. A non-cascade offer therefore has no setter of record, no default and no ceiling.

Verified verbatim in one file. 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:159 (States) and :123 both require '>=1 candidate and 0 triage actions' at 50% of the publish->decide-by window; :124 states 'dormant is a function of >=1 untriaged card, not of a percentage of the pile' for the poster who triaged 39 of 40. The two predicates are mutually exclusive at 39 actions, and neither carries a marker. The consequence is visible and load-bearing: the dormant signal drives the waiting-people nudge and feeds 04.05.01's detection of absence (:215), so one implementation never fires for a partly-triaged queue and the other fires on every queue with one card left.

Verified at 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:80-82 ('already eligible by construction ... never contains a mechanically-disqualified card'). 04.01.04 D-05 (:102) admits exactly such a card - 'The applicant may submit; the poster is shown the mismatch' - and enumerates it as a first-class applicant state, 'Invited-override ... No block; submit allowed with the unmet criterion shown honestly' (:74). The D-06 half is answered - 04.04.01:194 already binds bulk action to criteria live at submit time, which covers the tightening case - but the invite-waived card is not: it submitted while the criterion WAS live, so D-07's criterion-scoped bulk reject (:214) sweeps precisely the person the poster deliberately waived it for. Nothing in either file excludes them, and no marker records the interaction.

Verified at 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md D-11 (:255) - 'few values, never required, never free text' - with 'fee' appearing only inside copy at :143. The cited model does not supply the values: 04.05.01 D-03/D-10 and its reason table (:85-93) enumerate poster-side disposition values and three reason KINDS (criterion-scoped, structural, free text), none of which is a candidate-side decline vocabulary. The domain's own standard is enumeration - 04.05.01 lists all seven dispositions with setter and denominator columns, and 04.04.01:41-53 declares the hold blocker vocabulary 'closed' and lists all five with owner and resolution event. A closed set asserted with zero members, with no open question tracking it, while DT-15 (:219) calls this 'the most valuable signal in the domain'.

Verified: 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:79 makes delist 'Instant, always available', D-05 (:241) makes it never gated, and :185 hands the modelling away - 'Delisting is not a state of the obligation - it is a state of the slot.' A domain-wide grep shows 'delist' appears in no other file, including the lifecycle owner. 04.01.01's slot table (:228-233) has no delist trigger, and the nearest fit is foreclosed by its own text: Submission closed is triggered only by 'The post's date passed but the decide-by has not' and is expressly 'Only reachable where the two dates differ', which excludes a delisted dep call whose dates coincide. The post table (:235-247) likewise carries Withdrawn and Filled elsewhere but nothing for delist. A first-class, always-available act with no modelled effect on its object.

Verified at 04.05.03-won-opportunity-handoff.md:43-45 and D-12 (:241) versus the routing table at :52. The table proves it can express conditionals - the Session call row reads 'Join (or Create if no project exists)' - which makes the Dep/sub row's unconditional 'Join' a substantive assertion rather than shorthand. 04.01.01 D-02 (:307) guarantees the conflicting case exists and is complete ('Cold-typing remains complete - this feature does not require 17/18 to launch'), and a cold-typed dep call carries no target reference and no replaced-party reference, so the row's stated output - a substitution naming who came off - has no lineup to write to. Q-07 (:260) does not cover it: it fixes 'The requirement itself is not open' and defers only where the two fields land on the data model.
